newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi removes two senior U.S. oficials - Post.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi removes two senior U.S. oficials - Post.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motor Corp has replaced the two top Japanese officials at its U.S. auto operations, the Washington Post reported in its Tuesday editions.

The newspaper, quoting company officials, said the changes came just days after former U.S. Secretary of Labor Lynn Martin met with the parent company's board of directors in Tokyo to discuss progress being made on eliminating sexual harassment problems at the company's Normal, Illinois, plant.
Martin was hired last May to recommend workplace changes after the U.S. Equal Opportunity Employment Commission filed its biggest-ever sexual harassment case against the company.

The newspaper quoted a company source as saying the personnel changes had been made at the Illinois assembly plant out of concern that several key officials there -- both American and Japanese -- were resisting recommendations by a Martin-led task force to prevent harassment.

One of the officials being replaced last year organized a large employee demonstration outside the EEOC's Chicago offices to protest the lawsuit, which alleged that male employees and managers engaged in repeated acts of sexual harassment.
The company has denied that the sexual harassment was as widespread as the government claims.

Tsuneo Ohinouye, chairman of Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America, and Tohei Takeuchi, president of Mitsubishi Motor Sales of America, are both being replaced, effective June 27, company officials told the newspaper.
Their jobs would be combined under a new chairman, Michio Yamashita. The company source said he could make other personnel changes once he arrives.
The two men issued letters to their employees saying the changes were ordered by the parent company's board at its April 25 meeting. They will stay on as "advisers" to the company.
